title: PATH merge mode (ordered union + dedup) in systemd-envvar-sync
description:
## Summary
Add a MERGE mode for path-like vars so sync APPENDS-with-dedup instead of REPLACE. Core of the zse-mergeenv epic.

## Design
- New zstyle marks vars as path-like (colon-split, deduped):
  `zstyle ':zim:systemd-envvar:pathlike' vars PATH`
  (default just `PATH`; allow opt-in for PYTHONPATH/MANPATH/etc.)
- For each path-like var in the changed set, instead of `import-environment VAR`:
  1. read systemd's current value (`sd_env[VAR]`) and the shell's current value;
  2. build an ordered union: systemd entries first (preserve order), then shell entries not already present;
  3. dedup preserving first-seen order (zsh `typeset -U` on a tied array, or manual);
  4. `systemctl --user set-environment "VAR=<union>"` only if it differs from systemd's current.
- Non-path vars unchanged (import-environment replace).

## Acceptance
- systemd PATH is monotonic: entries already present are never dropped.
- Duplicates removed, first-seen order preserved.
- zstyle can add/remove path-like vars; PATH default-on.
- Unit tests: dedup, ordering, empty-systemd-value, empty-shell-value, idempotent (no set-environment when union unchanged).
- After running, systemd PATH gains `~/.local/share/pnpm/bin` (the currently-missing entry) and never loses it again.

title: Drop unexportable USERNAME; harden against non-exported params
description:
## Symptom
Every interactive shell prints: `Environment variable $USERNAME not set, ignoring.`

## Root cause
`general` group default is `HOME LANG TZ PAGER TERM PATH SHELL USER USERNAME LOGNAME`. zsh maintains `USERNAME` as a special parameter (auto-set from real UID via getpwuid) but does NOT export it. The sync does `systemctl --user import-environment USERNAME`; systemctl reads the inherited environ (no USERNAME there) -> warning. Since the import never succeeds, USERNAME always "differs" -> re-added every shell.

`USER` and `LOGNAME` are already in the group, both exported, both `rektide` -- so `USERNAME` is redundant on top of being broken.

## Fix (minimal)
In `functions/systemd-envvar-sync`, change the `general)` line to drop `USERNAME`:
`general) group_vars=(HOME LANG TZ PAGER TERM PATH SHELL USER LOGNAME) ;;`

## Fix (hardening, optional same PR)
Deeper bug: the function assumes every whitelisted name is exported. Guard the `changed` filter so only exported scalars are imported:
```
(( ${(P)+var} )) && [[ ${(t)var} == *export* ]] && [[ ${(P)var} != ${sd_env[$var]} ]] && changed+=$var
```
This skips special/non-exported params (USERNAME, UID, EUID, CPUTYPE, ...) before they reach systemctl.

## Acceptance
- No `$USERNAME not set, ignoring.` warning on shell start.
- USER and LOGNAME still imported into the systemd user env.

title: Merge/append env-var syncing instead of stomp
description:
## Background
zim-systemd-envvar pushes a curated whitelist of shell vars into the systemd user manager via `systemctl --user import-environment`. import-environment is full-REPLACE per variable: the systemd value becomes whatever the calling shell has, last-shell-wins.

## Problem
PATH (and other path-like vars) are not written, they are ACCUMULATED across many sources: .zshrc base (line 37), pnpm blocks (.zshrc:147 and :255-261, injected by compfuzor `pnpm.opt.pb`), `mise activate` (.zshenv/.zprofile), mise precmd (per-cwd tool paths), cargo, etc. Replace semantics therefore:
- drop entries an earlier shell had but the current shell lacks (last-shell-wins stomp);
- snapshot PATH too early: the sync runs at zim load (.zshrc:141), BEFORE the pnpm prepends at :147/:259, so systemd PATH is already stale — verified live: systemd is currently missing `~/.local/share/pnpm/bin`.

## Goal
Make sync MERGE / append-with-dedup for path-like vars the default, both:
1. in the shell-side `systemd-envvar-sync` function, and
2. as a REUSABLE helper for external service units (`mise-user-env`, `watchman-main`, `ssh-agent`, …) that want the same append-not-stomp behavior — using `ExecStartPre` (snapshot) + `ExecStartPost` (merge) so a unit's main `ExecStart` may stomp and the post step merges it back.

Keep an EAGER early sync so startup-time consumers see a populated env, then refine on first precmd once PATH is fully built. The merge helper makes doing both safe.

## Non-goals
- Not changing which vars are whitelisted by default (one removal tracked in `zse-username`).
- Not relocating .zshrc PATH assembly wholesale (tracked in `zse-zshrc-ownership` as exploration).

## Children
- `zse-username` — independent quick fix
- `zse-pathmerge` — core merge mode in the sync function
- `zse-mergehelper` — reusable helper + ExecStartPre/Post pattern
- `zse-timing` — eager early sync + first-precmd refresh

title: Eager early sync + first-precmd refresh to capture full PATH
description:
## Summary
Do BOTH: keep the eager init-time sync (so startup consumers get a populated env) AND add a once-only first-prompt refresh so the fully-built PATH is captured. Depends on zse-pathmerge (needs merge mode so the late refresh doesn't stomp).

## Why both
- Early only: PATH is incomplete -- sync currently fires at zim load (.zshrc:141), before pnpm (.zshrc:147/:259) and before mise precmd. systemd PATH misses entries (verified).
- Late only: scripts/services launched during shell startup see an empty/partial systemd env.
- Both: early gives a best-effort env immediately; late refines it to the true full PATH. Merge mode makes the late pass safe (append, not replace).

## Design
- Keep the direct `systemd-envvar-sync` call at module load (eager).
- Register a `precmd_functions` hook that:
  - runs once per shell (guard via a flag param),
  - is appended LATE in precmd_functions so it runs after mise's precmd (mise mutates PATH per-cwd on precmd),
  - calls `systemd-envvar-sync` again (now with merge mode + the complete PATH).
- The md5 cache already prevents redundant systemctl calls when nothing changed.

## precmd ordering note
zsh runs `precmd_functions` in array order. mise activate registers its own precmd; we must `precmd_functions+=(systemd-envvar-sync-precmd)` AFTER mise activates, or otherwise ensure we run last. Document this.

## Acceptance
- After first prompt, systemd PATH includes pnpm entries and any mise-precmd additions.
- Eager sync still happens at module load for early consumers.
- No re-import storm: second+ prompts no-op when env hash is stable.

title: Reusable merge-env helper for service units (ExecStartPre/Post pattern)
description:
## Summary
Extract the merge/dedup logic into a reusable helper that EXTERNAL service units can call, so units like mise-user-env, watchman-main, ssh-agent can do append-not-stomp too. Depends on zse-pathmerge (shares the dedup core).

## Two shapes to support

### Shape A: atomic single-call helper (preferred for new units)
`systemd-env-merge --pathlike PATH [--pathlike PYTHONPATH] -- KEY=VAL [KEY=VAL ...]`
- reads current `systemctl --user show-environment`,
- for path-like vars: ordered union (systemd first, then new VAL entries) with dedup,
- for the rest: plain replace,
- then one `set-environment` of the merged set.
The unit's ExecStart just calls this instead of `set-environment` directly. No pre/post needed.

### Shape B: ExecStartPre snapshot + ExecStartPost merge (retrofit existing stomping units)
For units that already do their own `set-environment`/`dbus-update-activation-environment` in ExecStart and we don't want to rewrite them:
- `ExecStartPre=` runs `systemd-env-snapshot /run/<unit>.env.snapshot [VAR...]` -> dump selected vars from `show-environment`.
- unit's `ExecStart=` runs unchanged (may stomp).
- `ExecStartPost=` runs `systemd-env-restore --pathlike PATH --merge /run/<unit>.env.snapshot` -> re-merge pre-state into post-state with dedup.
Note: both ExecStartPre and ExecStartPost run for a oneshot in the same activation, so the before/after pair is well-defined.

## Deliverable
- `bin/systemd-env-merge` (+ optional `systemd-env-snapshot`/`systemd-env-restore`), POSIX sh + jq, unit-testable.
- README section documenting both shapes and when to use each.
- Example: convert compfuzor `mise-user-env` (mise.opt.pb) to Shape A so its `mise-systemd-env.sh` merges instead of replaces (also lets it safely include PATH -- flip `mise_user_env_path: True`).

## Acceptance
- Helper works headless under systemd (mise/jq on /usr/bin PATH).
- Dedup behavior matches zse-pathmerge exactly (share code or share tests).
- mise-user-env using it: switching mise tool versions mid-session APPENDS the new install dir rather than replacing the whole PATH.

title: Should PATH-building move out of .zshrc into zim?
description:
## Question
We currently assemble PATH ad-hoc in .zshrc: base export (line 37), two pnpm blocks (:147, :255-261 injected by compfuzor `pnpm.opt.pb`), plus mise/cargo. The timing bugs in zse-timing stem from this -- the sync can't know when PATH is "done". Should stable PATH assembly move into a zim module so ordering is deterministic w.r.t. the sync?

## Options to evaluate
- A) A `zim-path` module that owns stable PATH entries (user-local, cargo, pnpm home) and runs before zim-systemd-envvar. .zshrc stops exporting PATH directly.
- B) Leave PATH in .zshrc; rely on zse-timing's deferred precmd to capture it. (status quo + fix)
- C) A compfuzor-orchestrated "PATH assembly" block-in-file that runs at END of .zshrc (after everything), with the sync deferred to after it.

## Note
This is cross-project (compfuzor owns the pnpm block-in-file; .zshrc itself is hand-maintained). Not blocking the merge work -- zse-timing makes the current layout safe regardless. Capture for later.

## Resolution
Pick A/B/C or explicit "won't fix". If A or C, file follow-ups in compfuzor.
